label: <DEL> step of long (L>=8) sequences whose first token is s (about to output s)
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (98% of mass), i.e. when the model is about to output the first original token, and only for long sequences (L=9 carries 64% of mass, L=8 34%, L=7 2%, never L<=6). Strongly selective for the first original token being s (86% of mass; rate 37x baseline). Predicate (DEL step, L>=8, orig(0)=s) gets precision 0.93, mass recall 0.82 on dev. Top activations often start with s s (a second s at position 1). Weak residual activations: DEL step with s at position 1 instead of 0, or other first tokens (w, v, a, b), and a few at the last original step (t=L-1) of L=9 sequences. Never fires in the copy phase or early original steps.

issues: Factual claims check out on the dev profile. Delimiter steps hold 98.1% of mass and copy-phase steps hold 0 (0 of 2.73M steps active). By length: L=9 holds 64.3%, L=8 33.8%, L=7 1.9%, L<=6 0. first_tok=s holds 86.1% of mass, and out_tok=s at the delimiter has 37x lift. orig_idx=8 (last original step of L=9) holds 1.9%.
Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.936, R 0.577, F1 0.713, mass recall 0.822.

The misses are weak and diffuse, not a sharp class. Delimiter steps at L>=8 whose first token is not s give precision 0.019 and 13.9% of mass. The largest structured part of that is orig(1)==s: precision 0.19 and 6.3% of mass. Adding it (restricted to L=9) raises mass recall to 0.87 but lowers test F1 to 0.693. Adding orig(1)==s for any L>=8 gives F1 0.627.

Widening the alternatives lowers test F1: L>=7 gives 0.643, and allowing first tokens {s, w, v} gives 0.478. Delimiter steps at L=7 with first token s fire only 14% of the time and carry 1.9% of mass. Requiring orig(0)=orig(1)=s gives precision 1.0 but only 5.8% mass recall, so it is a magnitude boost at most, which the explanation already flags as untested.

Activation strength depends on length within the predicate: L=9 precision is 0.99 vs 0.89 at L=8, and all 8 false positives shown are L=8. The explanation already says L=9 carries more mass, so this is a nuance rather than an error.
The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
